India Seizes Medical Equipment Firms' Sites Amid Ongoing Border Tensions

NEW DELHI, June 16 — Indian authorities have seized manufacturing sites belonging to several medical equipment and devices companies in the northern state of Punjab, following escalating cross-border tensions with a neighboring country. The move, announced by the Ministry of Home Affairs on Saturday, is part of a wider set of measures targeting firms with alleged foreign ties, and has sent shockwaves through the domestic medical equipment and devices industry.

At least five factories operated by major industry players, including Medigen Instruments Pvt Ltd and Surgitech Devices India, were sealed early Saturday. According to government officials, the seizures are intended “to safeguard national interests” and prevent potential technology transfer amid the current geopolitical standoff.

“The security situation requires decisive action,” a senior ministry official told reporters. “We are taking all necessary steps to ensure that sensitive technologies and equipment are not compromised.”

Industry sources estimate that over 2,700 workers have been locked out of their workplaces in the affected facilities since the sites were taken over by authorities. Trade unions representing employees at Medigen Instruments and Surgitech Devices have called on the government to clarify the duration of the measures and to provide for the welfare of displaced workers.

“We urge the authorities to expedite a resolution and to protect the livelihoods of thousands of skilled technicians and assembly-line staff,” said Usha Pal, president of the Punjab Medical Devices Workers Union. “Our members are deeply concerned about job security and loss of income.”

Analysts say the seizures could disrupt production of vital diagnostic and surgical equipment, with possible long-term effects on the industry’s growth. “This is a sector that has seen rapid expansion and investment in recent years,” said R.K. Desai, an industry analyst at India Market Insights. “The current uncertainty may dampen investor sentiment and slow ongoing projects.”

The Association of Indian Medical Equipment Manufacturers, in a statement released Sunday, called for dialogue between the government and industry stakeholders. “We recognize the importance of national security, but urge a balanced approach to minimize the impact on the sector’s workforce and production capabilities,” it said.

Authorities have not indicated when or if the seized sites will be returned to company control. As the situation remains fluid, industry leaders are bracing for further developments in the days ahead.
